capabilities.target: private repositories owned by the user

inputs.source: Issue bodies in the public repository, openable by any GitHub user

controls.name: Per-tool-call approval prompt (collapsed arguments)
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced outside the model, but the approver sees a model-authored, collapsed summary rather than the raw destination and payload, so a more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary can get exfiltration approved (ASI09). Runtime notes also record high approval volume per session, the approval-fatigue pattern (SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Per-repository scoped credential instead of an account-wide PAT
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped to only the public repository in use would make private-repository reads unreachable under any model behavior, severing the toxic combination at its source.

controls.name: Raw-action approval display (full diff and destination, not collapsed)
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the approver the actual destination repo and PR content, not a collapsed model summary, removes the model's ability to understate the action; effectiveness does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Pin GitHub MCP server image to a digest
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning the docker image by digest prevents the running server's tool definitions from changing without review, closing the rug-pull vector regardless of model capability.

findings.title: TC1 Lethal trifecta: untrusted issue content drives private repo read and public PR exfiltration

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled issue body in the public repo is read by the agent while it looks at open issues, and can contain injected instructions.
Agent follows injected instructions to read confidential content from a private repository, enabled because the single PAT has repo scope across all of the user's repos.
Agent opens a pull request on the public repository containing the private content, making it world-readable and effectively irreversible.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

findings.residual_rationale: The only preventive control is a per-call approval gate reviewed via collapsed, model-generated summaries (approval_review_mode: model_summary), which the rubric floors at moderate. Runtime notes record that users approve many calls per session with arguments collapsed by default, matching the approval-fatigue pattern (SAFE-T1403); the approver is not meaningfully evaluating each private-repo-read-then-public-PR request. Rated high rather than the moderate floor to reflect that fact.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval setting changed to batch or 'always allow' for this server, or the per-call prompt is removed; or the model is upgraded, making its collapsed summaries more persuasive at hiding the private-repo-to-public-PR step.

evidence.observation: Single docker-run GitHub MCP server configured with GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN as the only credential.
The personal access token has repo scope across every repository the user owns, public and private, so no credential boundary separates the public-repo task from private repos.
Anyone on GitHub can open issues in the public repository, making issue bodies an untrusted (U) input that enters the agent's context when it reviews open issues.
The client asks for approval per tool call, but arguments are collapsed by default and users approve many calls per session, the approval-fatigue pattern (SAFE-T1403).

recommendations.action: Scope the credential used for this agent to only the public repository being worked on, or use a repository-specific token/installation rather than an account-wide PAT.
Change the approval UI to show the raw destination repo and full diff/content by default rather than a collapsed model summary, especially for create_pull_request and any cross-repository read.
Add an automated check that flags or blocks pull requests whose content overlaps with text recently read from a different, more sensitive repository.

findings.title: ASI04: Unpinned GitHub MCP server image permits tool-definition rug pull (SAFE-T1201)

attack_path.note: docker run ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server with no tag or digest pin, so the image resolved can change between runs without review.

forecast.watch_signal: No digest pin added after this review; or the pulled image hash changes between sessions without an accompanying change log entry.

evidence.observation: The docker run args end with the bare image reference 'ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server' with no tag or digest, so Docker resolves to whatever 'latest' currently points to on each run.

recommendations.action: Pin the server image to a specific content digest and verify it before adopting updates.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted GitHub issue in the public repository can drive a single account-wide PAT to read confidential content from private repositories and then exfiltrate it by opening an irreversible, world-readable pull request on the public repository (TC1 lethal trifecta). The null step and runtime limits add the autonomy modifier. The only present control is a per-call approval prompt that shows a collapsed, model-authored summary and is, per the runtime notes, approved at high volume per session; this is rated high rather than the moderate floor a summary gate alone would produce, because the stated approval pattern is consistent with approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403, ASI09). A secondary, lower-confidence finding on the unpinned server image is rated separately. Forecast is critical: removing or loosening the approval gate (autonomy_increase, control_removal) or upgrading the model (more persuasive, better-hidden summaries) removes the only present control and returns exposure to its critical inherent level.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration shown in the artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No system prompt was supplied, so instruction-level issues (ambiguous goals, conflicting directives) could not be reviewed.

No audit logs or measured approval rates were provided; the approval-fatigue conclusion rests on the runtime note that users approve many calls per session with collapsed arguments, which is taken as given rather than independently verified.
Docker image pinning was assessed from the configuration file alone; the actual digest in use at runtime was not verified.
